SRC-372:R001.text: VERIFY STAGING INTEGRITY Read the actual per-file staging manifest and reconcile every current entry with index stages, blob hashes, paths, modes and source lineage. A previous report claimed index preservation even though reported before/after index identities differed. Determine whether these identifiers represent raw index bytes, derived snapshot IDs or other objects. Prove preservation with like-for-like raw byte hashes and independent manifest equality. If index bytes genuinely changed, investigate and report the actual mutation. Do not conceal it as an unchanged index.

SRC-372:R002.text: CLASSIFY OWNED CHANGES FOR RELEASE Separate SAIPEN implementation changes, other pending release cohorts, archived evidence and operational metadata. Review all remaining eligible SAIPEN-owned source changes. Determine their actual purpose, dependencies, tests, security implications and whether they are superseded. Do not assume all own-project files belong in the same public commit. Do not blindly publish operational evidence, private records, credentials, transient metadata or unrelated archival files. Associate each releasable change with a reviewed scope and verifiable source generation. Create canonical review evidence as required by existing policy. Do not self-certify independent approval.

SRC-372:R003.text: RECONCILE ALL REMOTES AND ANCESTRY Discover actual fetch/push URLs and exact branch destinations. Fetch remote refs without modifying the shared staging. Compare merge bases, reachability, ahead/behind relationships, unique commits, file changes and expected target branch. Do not assume a shorter or different SHA is necessarily newer. Do not assume that a commit absent from GitHub was lost or deleted; it may only exist in the local repository or another remote. Determine which existing remote is authoritative for the established public GitHub release. Respect any private-public boundary. Choose the safest supported non-destructive synchronization strategy: a separate worktree, integration branch, selective cherry-pick, reviewed patch transfer, or PR when required by branch protection. Never force-push, overwrite remote history, reset foreign state or blindly merge unrelated cohorts.

SRC-372:R004.text: CREATE AN ACTUALLY REVIEWED RELEASE COHORT A cohort with zero reviewed source paths is NOT release-ready. Resolve source dependencies and build an exact reviewed candidate. Run targeted verification while preparing the candidate, reconcile known baseline failures, and execute mandatory publication gates on the exact final source tree. Reject an unsafe public release even if focused tests pass. Publish only after the real existing broker authorizes the exact destination, branch, cohort, operation and relevant source identity. The operator's general maintenance preference is not a substitute for a cryptographic broker receipt. When broker approval is missing, prepare ONE exact approval packet via a supported host and leave the release ready without repeated free-form permission questions.

SRC-372:R005.text: VERIFY REAL GITHUB OUTCOME After a permitted publication, independently read the actual GitHub target branch from the remote service. Require the exact intended commit SHA or an explicitly supported, verified ancestry/merge outcome. Do not mark GitHub synchronized because an old cohort matches or because a remote tip merely changed.
